senses.gloss:
Bhūdevī
(‘the Earth-goddess’):
------------------------------------------
This earth which supports and sustains all the living beings has often been deified as the मोथेर्, Bhūmātā or Bhūmi-देवी or भूदेवी.
In the Hindu legends she is described as a daughter of ब्रह्मा, the Creator, and as a consort of विष्णु.
The Vaiṣṇava texts show her as the second consort of विष्णु, along with Śrīdevī or लक्ष्मी. Her other names are: Vasun-dharā, Dharaṇī, Medinī, Kṣoṇī and Pauṣṇī.
In इचोनोग्रफ्य् she is shown as a goddess with two hands, holding a red or a blue lotus in her right hand, while the left arm is gracefully hanging. She is on the left side of विष्णु. Her complexion may be white or golden.
Sometimes she is shown with four hands carrying a रत्नपात्र (jewel pot) in one hand, a pot filled with plants in the second, another pot filled with medicinal herbs in the third and a lotus in the last.
